Sutton's population increased by around 19,500 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 200,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Sutton increased by 10.3%, from just over 190,100 in 2011 to around 209,600 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of London (7.7%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Sutton was home to around 34.1 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 31.0 in 2011. This area was among the top 10% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Sutton than across London

Median age in Sutton

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Sutton increased by one year, from 38 to 39 years of age.

This area had a higher average (median) age than London as a whole in 2021 (35 years) but a slightly lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just under 6,300 (an increase of 19.2%), while the number of residents between 20 and 24 years fell by just over 700 (6.7% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.4 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Family in Sutton

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children increased in Sutton, but fell across England.

In Sutton, the percentage of households including a couple with dependent children rose from 22.4% in 2011 to 24.5% in 2021, while across England it fell from 19.3% to 18.9%. During the same period, the regional percentage increased from 17.8% to 18.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Sutton fell from 15.7% to 14.2%, while the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children increased from 6.8% to 7.5%.

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children in Sutton increased by 2.1 percentage points

Marriage and civil partnership in Sutton

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were married (or in a civil partnership) increased here, but fell across England.

In Sutton, the percentage that said they were married (or in a civil partnership) rose from 47.9% in 2011 to 48.4% in 2021, while across England it fell from 46.8% to 44.7%. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 40.2% to 40.0%.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Sutton increased from 34.7% to 36.4%, while the percentage of adults who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership decreased from 8.4% to 7.8%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who were married or in a civil partnership in Sutton increased by 0.5 percentage points

Employment in Sutton

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed fell in this area, but rose across London.

In Sutton, the percentage who were employed fell from 62.4% in 2011 to 61.6% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage increased from 58.6% to 59.4%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Sutton fell from 3.6% to 2.9%, while the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were retired (economically inactive) decreased from 18.2% to 17.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Sutton decreased by 0.9 percentage points

More adults worked short hours

In 2021, 10.3% of Sutton residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 9.0% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week was greater across London (1.9 percentage points, from 8.8% to 10.7%) than in Sutton (1.3 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Sutton increased by 1.3 percentage points

Sutton residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 148,200 Sutton residents said they were born in England. This represented 70.7% of the local population. The figure has decreased from just over 148,500 in 2011, which at the time represented 78.1% of Sutton's population.

India was the next most represented, with around 6,900 Sutton residents reporting this country of birth (3.3%). This figure was up from around 3,200 in 2011, which at the time represented 1.7% of the population of Sutton.

The number of Sutton residents born in Sri Lanka rose from around 3,400 in 2011 (1.8% of the local population) to around 4,600 in 2021 (2.2%).

In 2021, 70.7% of Sutton residents reported their country of birth as England

Disability in Sutton

In 2021, 6.4% of Sutton residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 7.4% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 11 people (8.9%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 9.1% in 2011. The proportion of Sutton residents who were not disabled increased from 83.4% to 84.7%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot was greater across London (2.3 percentage points, from 9.4% to 7.1%) than in Sutton (1.0 percentage points). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Sutton decreased by 1.0 percentage points

Unpaid care in Sutton

Sutton saw London's joint third-largest percentage-point fall (alongside Havering) in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care (from 7.3% in 2011 to 4.3% in 2021). These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

Across the region, only Redbridge (from 7.2% to 3.9%) and Harrow (from 7.5% to 4.4%) saw a greater decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care.

Every local authority area across London saw a fall in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care, as the regional proportion fell from 6.4% to 3.8%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Sutton decreased by 3.0 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Sutton

In 2021, 17.5% of Sutton residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 11.6% in 2011. The 6.0 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across London, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 18.5% to 20.7%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 68.3% of people in Sutton identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 78.6% in 2011), while 5.9% identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category (compared with 4.8% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category increased from 3.8% in 2011 to 4.8% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 17.5% of usual residents in Sutton identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

Health in Sutton

In 2021, 48.9% of Sutton residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 45.6% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 36.4% to 35.0%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Sutton residents describing their health as "very bad" remained 1.0%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.7% to 3.4%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Sutton increased by 3.3 percentage points

National identity in Sutton

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater in Sutton (2.4 percentage points) than across London (0.1 percentage points).

In Sutton, the percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity increased from 11.1% in 2011 to 13.5% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage increased from 22.4% to 22.5%.

The percentage of people who identified with a UK and non-UK national identity in Sutton increased from 1.4% to 3.8%, while the percentage of people who identified as "British only" increased from 21.6% to 56.4%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Sutton increased by 2.4 percentage points

Rise in private renting

Of Sutton households, 20.3% rented privately in 2021, up from 15.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in seven households (14.2%) lived in socially rented housing, compared with 14.6% in 2011. The percentage of Sutton households that owned their home (outright or with a mortgage or loan) decreased from 68.0% to 64.4%.

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater across London (4.9 percentage points, from 25.1% to 30.0%) than in Sutton (4.4 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.6 percentage points, from 16.8% to 20.5%.

Private renting in Sutton increased by 4.4 percentage points

Religion in Sutton

In 2021, 32.3% of Sutton residents reported having "No religion", up from 24.6% in 2011. The rise of 7.7 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Sutton. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across London, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 21.0% to 27.1%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 45.8% of people in Sutton described themselves as Christian (down from 58.4%), while 7.0% described themselves as Muslim (up from 4.1% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

In 2021, 32.3% of usual residents in Sutton reported having "No religion"
